prompt.content:
You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Failure checklist (before any candidate): unit mismatch (MW vs W, kJ vs J), fraction vs percent, K vs C; sign flip; swapped ports; wrong fluid class; efficiency > 1; out-of-range parameter; unconverged tear. Locate the failing check/stream first, fix it with the fewest edits, and never invent numbers.
Answer format (ledger): <diagnosis> citing only shown MW numbers, then <fix> with `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>`, `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`.

SKILL CATALOG (descriptions only; full text arrives as a tool result):
Primary skill for ledger: exergy-ledger: Use for ledger-repair tasks: the stream exergy lines E[x], component destruction lines ED[c], the constant T0, and how to find and fix a wrong line.
Use list_skills/load_skill to inspect a skill in full before applying it.
Available component skills (call load_skill(name) for the full text):
- absorption-chiller: Use when a plant contains an absorption_chiller (single-effect, hot-water driven) or when hot-water loops and chilled-water loops appear.
- combustor: Use when a plant contains a combustor: fuel and air burned to a set outlet temperature with pressure drop and heat loss, limited by oxygen, excess air and emissions.
- compressor: Use when a plant contains a compressor: gas compression by pressure ratio and isentropic efficiency, with surge and discharge-temperature limits.
- condenser: Use when a plant contains a condenser: a hot working fluid condenses into a cooling-water stream whose temperature rise sets the duty and approach.
- dc-load: Use when a plant contains a dc_load: the IT electrical demand, the fraction of its heat sent to coolant and the required coolant return temperature.
- district-heat: Use when a plant supplies district heat through an exhaust heat exchanger flagged useful or a heat pump lifting chiller rejection heat to the network.
- electric-chiller: Use when a plant contains an electric_chiller: vapour-compression cooling whose part-load COP depends on temperatures, approach and fouling.
- evaporator: Use when exhaust boils a working fluid in an orc_evaporator: bubble-point pinch, superheat, flow position, dryout and freeze limits.
- gas-engine: Use when a plant contains a gas_engine component: a reciprocating gas engine sized by rated electrical output, with air, fuel and exhaust ports.
- heat-pump: Use when a plant contains a heat_pump: heat lifted from a source stream to a hotter sink, limited by Lorenz COP, sink temperature, approach and lift.
- heat-pump-district-heat: Use when a plant delivers district heat, with a heat_pump on the chiller heat-rejection loop or a heat exchanger flagged useful_heat on the exhaust.
- heat-rejector: Use when a plant contains a heat_rejector (dry cooler or evaporative cooling tower) closing a cooling-water loop.
- hrsg: Use when a plant contains an hrsg: exhaust heats feedwater to steam at a set steam pressure, limited by the economiser approach, pinch and stack temperature.
- orc: Use when a plant has an organic Rankine cycle: an orc_evaporator and orc_turbine on exhaust heat, with fluid limits, pinch, flow position and a dry or wet expansion.
- orc-bottoming: Use when a plant contains an organic Rankine cycle (orc_evaporator, orc_turbine, pump, condenser) on exhaust heat.
- pump: Use when a plant contains a pump: liquid pressurisation by outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with NPSH, cavitation and two-phase-inlet limits.
- recuperator: Use when a plant contains a recuperator: two streams exchange heat to a set cold outlet with pressure drops, a minimum approach and an optional delivered-heat flag.
- turbine: Use when a plant contains a turbine: gas or steam expansion through an outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with backpressure and blade-temperature limits.

You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Failure checklist (before any candidate): unit mismatch (MW vs W, kJ vs J), fraction vs percent, K vs C; sign flip; swapped ports; wrong fluid class; efficiency > 1; out-of-range parameter; unconverged tear. You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).

prompt.content:
You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Failure checklist (before any candidate): unit mismatch (MW vs W, kJ vs J), fraction vs percent, K vs C; sign flip; swapped ports; wrong fluid class; efficiency > 1; out-of-range parameter; unconverged tear. Locate the failing check/stream first, fix it with the fewest edits, and never invent numbers.
Answer format (ledger): <diagnosis> citing only shown MW numbers, then <fix> with `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>`, `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`.

SKILL CATALOG (descriptions only; full text arrives as a tool result):
Primary skill for ledger: exergy-ledger: Use for ledger-repair tasks: the stream exergy lines E[x], component destruction lines ED[c], the constant T0, and how to find and fix a wrong line.
Use list_skills/load_skill to inspect a skill in full before applying it.
Available component skills (call load_skill(name) for the full text):
- absorption-chiller: Use when a plant contains an absorption_chiller (single-effect, hot-water driven) or when hot-water loops and chilled-water loops appear.
- combustor: Use when a plant contains a combustor: fuel and air burned to a set outlet temperature with pressure drop and heat loss, limited by oxygen, excess air and emissions.
- compressor: Use when a plant contains a compressor: gas compression by pressure ratio and isentropic efficiency, with surge and discharge-temperature limits.
- condenser: Use when a plant contains a condenser: a hot working fluid condenses into a cooling-water stream whose temperature rise sets the duty and approach.
- dc-load: Use when a plant contains a dc_load: the IT electrical demand, the fraction of its heat sent to coolant and the required coolant return temperature.
- district-heat: Use when a plant supplies district heat through an exhaust heat exchanger flagged useful or a heat pump lifting chiller rejection heat to the network.
- electric-chiller: Use when a plant contains an electric_chiller: vapour-compression cooling whose part-load COP depends on temperatures, approach and fouling.
- evaporator: Use when exhaust boils a working fluid in an orc_evaporator: bubble-point pinch, superheat, flow position, dryout and freeze limits.
- gas-engine: Use when a plant contains a gas_engine component: a reciprocating gas engine sized by rated electrical output, with air, fuel and exhaust ports.
- heat-pump: Use when a plant contains a heat_pump: heat lifted from a source stream to a hotter sink, limited by Lorenz COP, sink temperature, approach and lift.
- heat-pump-district-heat: Use when a plant delivers district heat, with a heat_pump on the chiller heat-rejection loop or a heat exchanger flagged useful_heat on the exhaust.
- heat-rejector: Use when a plant contains a heat_rejector (dry cooler or evaporative cooling tower) closing a cooling-water loop.
- hrsg: Use when a plant contains an hrsg: exhaust heats feedwater to steam at a set steam pressure, limited by the economiser approach, pinch and stack temperature.
- orc: Use when a plant has an organic Rankine cycle: an orc_evaporator and orc_turbine on exhaust heat, with fluid limits, pinch, flow position and a dry or wet expansion.
- orc-bottoming: Use when a plant contains an organic Rankine cycle (orc_evaporator, orc_turbine, pump, condenser) on exhaust heat.
- pump: Use when a plant contains a pump: liquid pressurisation by outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with NPSH, cavitation and two-phase-inlet limits.
- recuperator: Use when a plant contains a recuperator: two streams exchange heat to a set cold outlet with pressure drops, a minimum approach and an optional delivered-heat flag.
- turbine: Use when a plant contains a turbine: gas or steam expansion through an outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with backpressure and blade-temperature limits.

prompt.content:
You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Failure checklist (before any candidate): unit mismatch (MW vs W, kJ vs J), fraction vs percent, K vs C; sign flip; swapped ports; wrong fluid class; efficiency > 1; out-of-range parameter; unconverged tear. Locate the failing check/stream first, fix it with the fewest edits, and never invent numbers.
Answer format (ledger): <diagnosis> citing only shown MW numbers, then <fix> with `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>`, `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`.

- absorption-chiller: Use when a plant contains an absorption_chiller (single-effect, hot-water driven) or when hot-water loops and chilled-water loops appear.

- condenser: Use when a plant contains a condenser: a hot working fluid condenses into a cooling-water stream whose temperature rise sets the duty and approach.
- dc-load: Use when a plant contains a dc_load: the IT electrical demand, the fraction of its heat sent to coolant and the required coolant return temperature.

- electric-chiller: Use when a plant contains an electric_chiller: vapour-compression cooling whose part-load COP depends on temperatures, approach and fouling.
- evaporator: Use when exhaust boils a working fluid in an orc_evaporator: bubble-point pinch, superheat, flow position, dryout and freeze limits.

A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).

prompt.content:
You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Failure checklist (before any candidate): unit mismatch (MW vs W, kJ vs J), fraction vs percent, K vs C; sign flip; swapped ports; wrong fluid class; efficiency > 1; out-of-range parameter; unconverged tear. Locate the failing check/stream first, fix it with the fewest edits, and never invent numbers.
Answer format (ledger): <diagnosis> citing only shown MW numbers, then <fix> with `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>`, `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`.

SKILL CATALOG (descriptions only; full text arrives as a tool result):
Primary skill for ledger: exergy-ledger: Use for ledger-repair tasks: the stream exergy lines E[x], component destruction lines ED[c], the constant T0, and how to find and fix a wrong line.
Use list_skills/load_skill to inspect a skill in full before applying it.
Available component skills (call load_skill(name) for the full text):
- absorption-chiller: Use when a plant contains an absorption_chiller (single-effect, hot-water driven) or when hot-water loops and chilled-water loops appear.
- combustor: Use when a plant contains a combustor: fuel and air burned to a set outlet temperature with pressure drop and heat loss, limited by oxygen, excess air and emissions.
- compressor: Use when a plant contains a compressor: gas compression by pressure ratio and isentropic efficiency, with surge and discharge-temperature limits.
- condenser: Use when a plant contains a condenser: a hot working fluid condenses into a cooling-water stream whose temperature rise sets the duty and approach.
- dc-load: Use when a plant contains a dc_load: the IT electrical demand, the fraction of its heat sent to coolant and the required coolant return temperature.
- district-heat: Use when a plant supplies district heat through an exhaust heat exchanger flagged useful or a heat pump lifting chiller rejection heat to the network.
- electric-chiller: Use when a plant contains an electric_chiller: vapour-compression cooling whose part-load COP depends on temperatures, approach and fouling.
- evaporator: Use when exhaust boils a working fluid in an orc_evaporator: bubble-point pinch, superheat, flow position, dryout and freeze limits.
- gas-engine: Use when a plant contains a gas_engine component: a reciprocating gas engine sized by rated electrical output, with air, fuel and exhaust ports.
- heat-pump: Use when a plant contains a heat_pump: heat lifted from a source stream to a hotter sink, limited by Lorenz COP, sink temperature, approach and lift.
- heat-pump-district-heat: Use when a plant delivers district heat, with a heat_pump on the chiller heat-rejection loop or a heat exchanger flagged useful_heat on the exhaust.
- heat-rejector: Use when a plant contains a heat_rejector (dry cooler or evaporative cooling tower) closing a cooling-water loop.
- hrsg: Use when a plant contains an hrsg: exhaust heats feedwater to steam at a set steam pressure, limited by the economiser approach, pinch and stack temperature.
- orc: Use when a plant has an organic Rankine cycle: an orc_evaporator and orc_turbine on exhaust heat, with fluid limits, pinch, flow position and a dry or wet expansion.

- pump: Use when a plant contains a pump: liquid pressurisation by outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with NPSH, cavitation and two-phase-inlet limits.
- recuperator: Use when a plant contains a recuperator: two streams exchange heat to a set cold outlet with pressure drops, a minimum approach and an optional delivered-heat flag.

prompt.content:
You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Failure checklist (before any candidate): unit mismatch (MW vs W, kJ vs J), fraction vs percent, K vs C; sign flip; swapped ports; wrong fluid class; efficiency > 1; out-of-range parameter; unconverged tear. Locate the failing check/stream first, fix it with the fewest edits, and never invent numbers.
Answer format (ledger): <diagnosis> citing only shown MW numbers, then <fix> with `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>`, `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`.

- condenser: Use when a plant contains a condenser: a hot working fluid condenses into a cooling-water stream whose temperature rise sets the duty and approach.
- dc-load: Use when a plant contains a dc_load: the IT electrical demand, the fraction of its heat sent to coolant and the required coolant return temperature.

- gas-engine: Use when a plant contains a gas_engine component: a reciprocating gas engine sized by rated electrical output, with air, fuel and exhaust ports.

A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. prompt.content:
You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Failure checklist (before any candidate): unit mismatch (MW vs W, kJ vs J), fraction vs percent, K vs C; sign flip; swapped ports; wrong fluid class; efficiency > 1; out-of-range parameter; unconverged tear. Locate the failing check/stream first, fix it with the fewest edits, and never invent numbers.
Answer format (ledger): <diagnosis> citing only shown MW numbers, then <fix> with `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>`, `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`.

SKILL CATALOG (descriptions only; full text arrives as a tool result):
Primary skill for ledger: exergy-ledger: Use for ledger-repair tasks: the stream exergy lines E[x], component destruction lines ED[c], the constant T0, and how to find and fix a wrong line.
Use list_skills/load_skill to inspect a skill in full before applying it.
Available component skills (call load_skill(name) for the full text):
- absorption-chiller: Use when a plant contains an absorption_chiller (single-effect, hot-water driven) or when hot-water loops and chilled-water loops appear.
- combustor: Use when a plant contains a combustor: fuel and air burned to a set outlet temperature with pressure drop and heat loss, limited by oxygen, excess air and emissions.
- compressor: Use when a plant contains a compressor: gas compression by pressure ratio and isentropic efficiency, with surge and discharge-temperature limits.
- condenser: Use when a plant contains a condenser: a hot working fluid condenses into a cooling-water stream whose temperature rise sets the duty and approach.
- dc-load: Use when a plant contains a dc_load: the IT electrical demand, the fraction of its heat sent to coolant and the required coolant return temperature.
- district-heat: Use when a plant supplies district heat through an exhaust heat exchanger flagged useful or a heat pump lifting chiller rejection heat to the network.
- electric-chiller: Use when a plant contains an electric_chiller: vapour-compression cooling whose part-load COP depends on temperatures, approach and fouling.
- evaporator: Use when exhaust boils a working fluid in an orc_evaporator: bubble-point pinch, superheat, flow position, dryout and freeze limits.
- gas-engine: Use when a plant contains a gas_engine component: a reciprocating gas engine sized by rated electrical output, with air, fuel and exhaust ports.
- heat-pump: Use when a plant contains a heat_pump: heat lifted from a source stream to a hotter sink, limited by Lorenz COP, sink temperature, approach and lift.
- heat-pump-district-heat: Use when a plant delivers district heat, with a heat_pump on the chiller heat-rejection loop or a heat exchanger flagged useful_heat on the exhaust.
- heat-rejector: Use when a plant contains a heat_rejector (dry cooler or evaporative cooling tower) closing a cooling-water loop.

- recuperator: Use when a plant contains a recuperator: two streams exchange heat to a set cold outlet with pressure drops, a minimum approach and an optional delivered-heat flag.

You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Failure checklist (before any candidate): unit mismatch (MW vs W, kJ vs J), fraction vs percent, K vs C; sign flip; swapped ports; wrong fluid class; efficiency > 1; out-of-range parameter; unconverged tear. Locate the failing check/stream first, fix it with the fewest edits, and never invent numbers.

prompt.content:
You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Failure checklist (before any candidate): unit mismatch (MW vs W, kJ vs J), fraction vs percent, K vs C; sign flip; swapped ports; wrong fluid class; efficiency > 1; out-of-range parameter; unconverged tear. Locate the failing check/stream first, fix it with the fewest edits, and never invent numbers.
Answer format (ledger): <diagnosis> citing only shown MW numbers, then <fix> with `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>`, `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`.

SKILL CATALOG (descriptions only; full text arrives as a tool result):
Primary skill for ledger: exergy-ledger: Use for ledger-repair tasks: the stream exergy lines E[x], component destruction lines ED[c], the constant T0, and how to find and fix a wrong line.
Use list_skills/load_skill to inspect a skill in full before applying it.
Available component skills (call load_skill(name) for the full text):
- absorption-chiller: Use when a plant contains an absorption_chiller (single-effect, hot-water driven) or when hot-water loops and chilled-water loops appear.
- combustor: Use when a plant contains a combustor: fuel and air burned to a set outlet temperature with pressure drop and heat loss, limited by oxygen, excess air and emissions.
- compressor: Use when a plant contains a compressor: gas compression by pressure ratio and isentropic efficiency, with surge and discharge-temperature limits.
- condenser: Use when a plant contains a condenser: a hot working fluid condenses into a cooling-water stream whose temperature rise sets the duty and approach.
- dc-load: Use when a plant contains a dc_load: the IT electrical demand, the fraction of its heat sent to coolant and the required coolant return temperature.
- district-heat: Use when a plant supplies district heat through an exhaust heat exchanger flagged useful or a heat pump lifting chiller rejection heat to the network.
- electric-chiller: Use when a plant contains an electric_chiller: vapour-compression cooling whose part-load COP depends on temperatures, approach and fouling.
- evaporator: Use when exhaust boils a working fluid in an orc_evaporator: bubble-point pinch, superheat, flow position, dryout and freeze limits.
- gas-engine: Use when a plant contains a gas_engine component: a reciprocating gas engine sized by rated electrical output, with air, fuel and exhaust ports.
- heat-pump: Use when a plant contains a heat_pump: heat lifted from a source stream to a hotter sink, limited by Lorenz COP, sink temperature, approach and lift.
- heat-pump-district-heat: Use when a plant delivers district heat, with a heat_pump on the chiller heat-rejection loop or a heat exchanger flagged useful_heat on the exhaust.
- heat-rejector: Use when a plant contains a heat_rejector (dry cooler or evaporative cooling tower) closing a cooling-water loop.
- hrsg: Use when a plant contains an hrsg: exhaust heats feedwater to steam at a set steam pressure, limited by the economiser approach, pinch and stack temperature.
- orc: Use when a plant has an organic Rankine cycle: an orc_evaporator and orc_turbine on exhaust heat, with fluid limits, pinch, flow position and a dry or wet expansion.
- orc-bottoming: Use when a plant contains an organic Rankine cycle (orc_evaporator, orc_turbine, pump, condenser) on exhaust heat.
- pump: Use when a plant contains a pump: liquid pressurisation by outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with NPSH, cavitation and two-phase-inlet limits.
- recuperator: Use when a plant contains a recuperator: two streams exchange heat to a set cold outlet with pressure drops, a minimum approach and an optional delivered-heat flag.
- turbine: Use when a plant contains a turbine: gas or steam expansion through an outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with backpressure and blade-temperature limits.

A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. prompt.content:
You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Failure checklist (before any candidate): unit mismatch (MW vs W, kJ vs J), fraction vs percent, K vs C; sign flip; swapped ports; wrong fluid class; efficiency > 1; out-of-range parameter; unconverged tear. Locate the failing check/stream first, fix it with the fewest edits, and never invent numbers.
Answer format (ledger): <diagnosis> citing only shown MW numbers, then <fix> with `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>`, `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`.

SKILL CATALOG (descriptions only; full text arrives as a tool result):
Primary skill for ledger: exergy-ledger: Use for ledger-repair tasks: the stream exergy lines E[x], component destruction lines ED[c], the constant T0, and how to find and fix a wrong line.
Use list_skills/load_skill to inspect a skill in full before applying it.
Available component skills (call load_skill(name) for the full text):
- absorption-chiller: Use when a plant contains an absorption_chiller (single-effect, hot-water driven) or when hot-water loops and chilled-water loops appear.
- combustor: Use when a plant contains a combustor: fuel and air burned to a set outlet temperature with pressure drop and heat loss, limited by oxygen, excess air and emissions.
- compressor: Use when a plant contains a compressor: gas compression by pressure ratio and isentropic efficiency, with surge and discharge-temperature limits.
- condenser: Use when a plant contains a condenser: a hot working fluid condenses into a cooling-water stream whose temperature rise sets the duty and approach.
- dc-load: Use when a plant contains a dc_load: the IT electrical demand, the fraction of its heat sent to coolant and the required coolant return temperature.
- district-heat: Use when a plant supplies district heat through an exhaust heat exchanger flagged useful or a heat pump lifting chiller rejection heat to the network.
- electric-chiller: Use when a plant contains an electric_chiller: vapour-compression cooling whose part-load COP depends on temperatures, approach and fouling.
- evaporator: Use when exhaust boils a working fluid in an orc_evaporator: bubble-point pinch, superheat, flow position, dryout and freeze limits.
- gas-engine: Use when a plant contains a gas_engine component: a reciprocating gas engine sized by rated electrical output, with air, fuel and exhaust ports.
- heat-pump: Use when a plant contains a heat_pump: heat lifted from a source stream to a hotter sink, limited by Lorenz COP, sink temperature, approach and lift.
- heat-pump-district-heat: Use when a plant delivers district heat, with a heat_pump on the chiller heat-rejection loop or a heat exchanger flagged useful_heat on the exhaust.
- heat-rejector: Use when a plant contains a heat_rejector (dry cooler or evaporative cooling tower) closing a cooling-water loop.
- hrsg: Use when a plant contains an hrsg: exhaust heats feedwater to steam at a set steam pressure, limited by the economiser approach, pinch and stack temperature.
- orc: Use when a plant has an organic Rankine cycle: an orc_evaporator and orc_turbine on exhaust heat, with fluid limits, pinch, flow position and a dry or wet expansion.
- orc-bottoming: Use when a plant contains an organic Rankine cycle (orc_evaporator, orc_turbine, pump, condenser) on exhaust heat.
- pump: Use when a plant contains a pump: liquid pressurisation by outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with NPSH, cavitation and two-phase-inlet limits.
- recuperator: Use when a plant contains a recuperator: two streams exchange heat to a set cold outlet with pressure drops, a minimum approach and an optional delivered-heat flag.
- turbine: Use when a plant contains a turbine: gas or steam expansion through an outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with backpressure and blade-temperature limits.

A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).

You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Failure checklist (before any candidate): unit mismatch (MW vs W, kJ vs J), fraction vs percent, K vs C; sign flip; swapped ports; wrong fluid class; efficiency > 1; out-of-range parameter; unconverged tear. You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. prompt.content:
You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Failure checklist (before any candidate): unit mismatch (MW vs W, kJ vs J), fraction vs percent, K vs C; sign flip; swapped ports; wrong fluid class; efficiency > 1; out-of-range parameter; unconverged tear. Locate the failing check/stream first, fix it with the fewest edits, and never invent numbers.
Answer format (ledger): <diagnosis> citing only shown MW numbers, then <fix> with `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>`, `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`.

SKILL CATALOG (descriptions only; full text arrives as a tool result):
Primary skill for ledger: exergy-ledger: Use for ledger-repair tasks: the stream exergy lines E[x], component destruction lines ED[c], the constant T0, and how to find and fix a wrong line.
Use list_skills/load_skill to inspect a skill in full before applying it.
Available component skills (call load_skill(name) for the full text):
- absorption-chiller: Use when a plant contains an absorption_chiller (single-effect, hot-water driven) or when hot-water loops and chilled-water loops appear.
- combustor: Use when a plant contains a combustor: fuel and air burned to a set outlet temperature with pressure drop and heat loss, limited by oxygen, excess air and emissions.
- compressor: Use when a plant contains a compressor: gas compression by pressure ratio and isentropic efficiency, with surge and discharge-temperature limits.
- condenser: Use when a plant contains a condenser: a hot working fluid condenses into a cooling-water stream whose temperature rise sets the duty and approach.
- dc-load: Use when a plant contains a dc_load: the IT electrical demand, the fraction of its heat sent to coolant and the required coolant return temperature.
- district-heat: Use when a plant supplies district heat through an exhaust heat exchanger flagged useful or a heat pump lifting chiller rejection heat to the network.
- electric-chiller: Use when a plant contains an electric_chiller: vapour-compression cooling whose part-load COP depends on temperatures, approach and fouling.
- evaporator: Use when exhaust boils a working fluid in an orc_evaporator: bubble-point pinch, superheat, flow position, dryout and freeze limits.
- gas-engine: Use when a plant contains a gas_engine component: a reciprocating gas engine sized by rated electrical output, with air, fuel and exhaust ports.
- heat-pump: Use when a plant contains a heat_pump: heat lifted from a source stream to a hotter sink, limited by Lorenz COP, sink temperature, approach and lift.

- recuperator: Use when a plant contains a recuperator: two streams exchange heat to a set cold outlet with pressure drops, a minimum approach and an optional delivered-heat flag.

You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Failure checklist (before any candidate): unit mismatch (MW vs W, kJ vs J), fraction vs percent, K vs C; sign flip; swapped ports; wrong fluid class; efficiency > 1; out-of-range parameter; unconverged tear. prompt.content:
You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Failure checklist (before any candidate): unit mismatch (MW vs W, kJ vs J), fraction vs percent, K vs C; sign flip; swapped ports; wrong fluid class; efficiency > 1; out-of-range parameter; unconverged tear. Locate the failing check/stream first, fix it with the fewest edits, and never invent numbers.
Answer format (ledger): <diagnosis> citing only shown MW numbers, then <fix> with `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>`, `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`.

Primary skill for ledger: exergy-ledger: Use for ledger-repair tasks: the stream exergy lines E[x], component destruction lines ED[c], the constant T0, and how to find and fix a wrong line.
Use list_skills/load_skill to inspect a skill in full before applying it.
Available component skills (call load_skill(name) for the full text):
- absorption-chiller: Use when a plant contains an absorption_chiller (single-effect, hot-water driven) or when hot-water loops and chilled-water loops appear.
- combustor: Use when a plant contains a combustor: fuel and air burned to a set outlet temperature with pressure drop and heat loss, limited by oxygen, excess air and emissions.
- compressor: Use when a plant contains a compressor: gas compression by pressure ratio and isentropic efficiency, with surge and discharge-temperature limits.
- condenser: Use when a plant contains a condenser: a hot working fluid condenses into a cooling-water stream whose temperature rise sets the duty and approach.
- dc-load: Use when a plant contains a dc_load: the IT electrical demand, the fraction of its heat sent to coolant and the required coolant return temperature.
- district-heat: Use when a plant supplies district heat through an exhaust heat exchanger flagged useful or a heat pump lifting chiller rejection heat to the network.
- electric-chiller: Use when a plant contains an electric_chiller: vapour-compression cooling whose part-load COP depends on temperatures, approach and fouling.
- evaporator: Use when exhaust boils a working fluid in an orc_evaporator: bubble-point pinch, superheat, flow position, dryout and freeze limits.

You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Failure checklist (before any candidate): unit mismatch (MW vs W, kJ vs J), fraction vs percent, K vs C; sign flip; swapped ports; wrong fluid class; efficiency > 1; out-of-range parameter; unconverged tear. Locate the failing check/stream first, fix it with the fewest edits, and never invent numbers.

You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Failure checklist (before any candidate): unit mismatch (MW vs W, kJ vs J), fraction vs percent, K vs C; sign flip; swapped ports; wrong fluid class; efficiency > 1; out-of-range parameter; unconverged tear. You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).

A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).

You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Failure checklist (before any candidate): unit mismatch (MW vs W, kJ vs J), fraction vs percent, K vs C; sign flip; swapped ports; wrong fluid class; efficiency > 1; out-of-range parameter; unconverged tear. Locate the failing check/stream first, fix it with the fewest edits, and never invent numbers.

prompt.content:
You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Failure checklist (before any candidate): unit mismatch (MW vs W, kJ vs J), fraction vs percent, K vs C; sign flip; swapped ports; wrong fluid class; efficiency > 1; out-of-range parameter; unconverged tear. Locate the failing check/stream first, fix it with the fewest edits, and never invent numbers.
Answer format (ledger): <diagnosis> citing only shown MW numbers, then <fix> with `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>`, `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`.

- condenser: Use when a plant contains a condenser: a hot working fluid condenses into a cooling-water stream whose temperature rise sets the duty and approach.

You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. prompt.content:
You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Failure checklist (before any candidate): unit mismatch (MW vs W, kJ vs J), fraction vs percent, K vs C; sign flip; swapped ports; wrong fluid class; efficiency > 1; out-of-range parameter; unconverged tear. Locate the failing check/stream first, fix it with the fewest edits, and never invent numbers.

You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Failure checklist (before any candidate): unit mismatch (MW vs W, kJ vs J), fraction vs percent, K vs C; sign flip; swapped ports; wrong fluid class; efficiency > 1; out-of-range parameter; unconverged tear. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).

prompt.content:
You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Failure checklist (before any candidate): unit mismatch (MW vs W, kJ vs J), fraction vs percent, K vs C; sign flip; swapped ports; wrong fluid class; efficiency > 1; out-of-range parameter; unconverged tear. Locate the failing check/stream first, fix it with the fewest edits, and never invent numbers.
Answer format (ledger): <diagnosis> citing only shown MW numbers, then <fix> with `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>`, `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`.

Available component skills (call load_skill(name) for the full text):
- absorption-chiller: Use when a plant contains an absorption_chiller (single-effect, hot-water driven) or when hot-water loops and chilled-water loops appear.

- condenser: Use when a plant contains a condenser: a hot working fluid condenses into a cooling-water stream whose temperature rise sets the duty and approach.
- dc-load: Use when a plant contains a dc_load: the IT electrical demand, the fraction of its heat sent to coolant and the required coolant return temperature.
- district-heat: Use when a plant supplies district heat through an exhaust heat exchanger flagged useful or a heat pump lifting chiller rejection heat to the network.
- electric-chiller: Use when a plant contains an electric_chiller: vapour-compression cooling whose part-load COP depends on temperatures, approach and fouling.

You debug exergy ledgers of energy plants. A ledger computes the exergy flow E[x] (MW) of every stream x from its state values, and the exergy destruction ED[c] (MW) of every component c as the exergy of its inlet streams minus the exergy of its outlet streams minus the work it delivers. A correct ledger gives ED >= 0 for every component and closes: the sum of all ED equals the exergy entering at the boundaries minus the exergy leaving minus the net work. You are given the ledger, the topology, the values and the result. Answer with a short <diagnosis> citing only numbers shown (MW), then <fix> with at most 4 lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>` or `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`. Expressions use numbers, + - * /, parentheses, T0, and lookups m[x], h[x], s[x], g0[x], ech[x], E[x], W[c]. Change only what is wrong.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Failure checklist (before any candidate): unit mismatch (MW vs W, kJ vs J), fraction vs percent, K vs C; sign flip; swapped ports; wrong fluid class; efficiency > 1; out-of-range parameter; unconverged tear.
